Welcome to Rhino Post Safari Lodge
Experience the true beauty of the Kruger
Home / Our Lodges / Welcome to Rhino Post Safari Lodge
Situated on a 12000-hectare concession in the south-western section of the Kruger National Park, Rhino Post Safari Lodge offers an unforgettable African safari experience. The private concession borders Mala Mala and Sabi Sands Private Game Reserves and allows the unrestricted passage for a variety of animals and wildlife to wander through, creating moments of wonder for all our guests.
Become one with nature
The lodge overlooks the perennially dry Mutlumuvi riverbed. With wooden decks built around a forest of riverine trees, shade is plentiful. Raised wooden walkways link eight thatched suites each offering their own outdoor shower and private deck. Our lodge is designed with vast areas of open space, large glass doors and windows helping to bring the outside in. Wherever you are – at the pool, the bar, in the lounge, taking a bath or shower, or just relaxing in your room, we endeavour to make you feel as if you are always at one with nature.
Take a moment to yourself
The lounge bar and viewing deck are sizable enough to be both social and cosy and at the same time, large enough that guests are able to enjoy some quiet-time and solitude. The reception and curio shop are combined to ensure that there is always someone to attend to your needs, whether you are booking an in-room massage therapy or picking out gifts for loved ones at home.
There is always time for more
Our early morning game drives (safaris) are long enough to be able to view a substantial amount of game, yet short enough to enjoy a leisurely brunch, swim, massage or afternoon nap before high tea and a late afternoon drive.
Our evening safari is highlighted by sundowner drinks, after which we drive back to the lodge for pre-dinner drinks and a delicious dinner. Whether you are planning to spend as much time as possible out on drives, or just to relax and unwind in the lodge, you will be immersed in nature at all times.
Private Decks
Eight suites each with a Private Deck and outdoor shower overlooking the Mutlumuvi Riverbed
Firepit
Open Plan lounge and deck with a recessed fire pit overlooking an active waterhole
Room for everyone
Ample seating on the Main Deck
Take a dip
The secluded swimming pool area overlooks a waterhole and offers an opportunity for a refreshing break
A roof of stars
Indoor and outdoor dining (weather permitting) allowing you to enjoy alfresco dining under the stars
Take a bit of Africa home
Our curio shop offers a wide variety of momentos, souveniers and gifts for all ages
A bar with a view
Our unique bar, handmade from a variety of local woods, boasts the best view of the waterhole and opportunity to watch animals go by
A massage to remember
In-room massage therapies are the perfect bush pamper
Star gazing
Our telescope is available for all guests and offers a magnificent view of the African skies at night

Wander up an old elephant path, to the top of a small slope where the swimming pool is carefully positioned with a view of a popular waterhole. Enjoy a refreshing swim or laze in the sun or shade between game drives.
A toast to Africa
Our wine cellar carries a wide selection of South African wines from crisp, dry whites to gentle fruity Rosé or Methode Cap Classique Sparkling Wines perfect for a warm summer’s day. In winter soothing sherry and fortified wines are the order of the day. The toughest decision of your day being whether to complement your evening meal with a full-bodied Merlot, robust Cabernet Sauvignon or flamboyant Pinotage.
The best view in town
Our bar area and firepit overlook a waterhole filled from a borehole providing a refreshing stop for thirsty elephant and antelope in summer and a significant water source for a wide variety of animals in the dry winter months. Enjoy sipping on a cocktail while keeping an eye on the variety of wildlife as they slake their thirst. If you’re a true connoisseur, enjoy a South African speciality, Six Dogs Gin on a balmy summer evening, or a speciality espresso with or without a dash of Amarula Cream on a chilly winter’s night.
Share a meal, share a memory

AN ISLAND SAFARI ON THE BANKS OF THE ZAMBEZI
Chundu Island, Zimbabwe
Just 21 kilometres upstream from the iconic Victoria Falls,  Chundu  Island is a secluded  private island  lodge set in the middle of the powerful Zambezi River, surrounded by the wilderness of Zambezi National Park on the natural border between Zimbabwe and Zambia. Eight spacious, Seychelles-inspired river suites sit right along the water s edge, offering privacy, sweeping views and the soothing soundtrack of the Zambezi flowing past. Part of the  Seolo  Africa collection,  Chundu  Island blends relaxed island living with classic safari adventure, from game drives and guided walks to fishing,  canoeing  and river cruises.
Chundu Island Book Now
OUR PREFERRED PARTNER FOR SAFARI EXPERIENCE IN ZIMBABWE
Masuwe Lodge, Victoria Falls
Just 7 km from the world-famous Victoria Falls,  Masuwe  Lodge offers a peaceful retreat where guests can experience both the energy of the Falls and the quiet beauty of the surrounding wilderness. Set within its own private sanctuary and close to the wild landscapes of Zambezi National Park, the lodge, part of  Seolo  Africa s collection, blends relaxed bush living with easy access to one of Africa s most iconic destinations. Enjoy game drives across the  Chamabonda   vlei , guided walks through the  Masuwe  Sanctuary, and rewarding birdwatching, all from a choice of three distinct accommodation styles.
Masuwe Lodge Book Now
AN AUTHENTIC SOUTHERN AFRICAN SAFARI ADVENTURE
Rhino Post Safari Lodge, Kruger Park
Named for a wooden post once polished smooth by a passing rhino, Rhino Post Safari Lodge is a tranquil hideaway deep within Kruger National Park, overlooking the usually dry Mutlumuvi  riverbed. Eight spacious suites, crafted from stone, wood and other natural materials, blend into their surroundings while keeping the lodge s footprint refreshingly light. Morning and evening game drives roam both Rhino Post s private concession and Kruger s public roads, delivering  incredible  wildlife encounters. For something extra, sleep out beneath the stars on  the Sleep-Out Decks , or tee off at Skukuza Golf Club, famously the wildest course in the world.
Rhino Post Safari Lodge Book Now
A SAFARI ADVENTURE YOU WILL NEVER FORGET
Plains Camp @ Rhino Walking Safaris, Kruger Park
Set within a thicket of  knobthorn  trees on the edge of an open plain in Kruger National Park, Plains Camp @ Rhino Walking Safaris offers an intimate, immersive wilderness experience built for just eight guests at a time across four stylish en-suite safari tents. As one of the few  specialist  walking safari operations in Kruger, guests are  led  on foot by highly trained, armed guides who reveal the tracks, wildlife and plant life that make up the true rhythm of the bush. For the ultimate night out, walk to the elevated sleep-out decks above the  Xiteveteve  waterhole and sleep under the stars.
Rhino Walking Safaris Book Now
THE ULTIMATE ACTIVITY
Sleep out under the African sky
For the adventurous, a night out at the Sleep-Out Decks can be booked, where a guide cooks a traditional South African “braai” over an open fire, and the night is spent under the stars listening to the night sounds so far removed from civilization. We are delighted to be able to share this matchless blend of Kruger in style with our many return guests and supporters of ethical and responsible environmental tourism.
Sleep-Outs
Our Safari Siblings
Safari Siblings represent individuals we entrust not just with our guests experiences but also with the preservation of nature and the promotion of sustainable tourism. We ve meticulously chosen partners and properties whose values align with ours, ensuring they provide genuine, high-quality experiences that harmonise with the destinations we curate.

Masuwe Lodge, Victoria Falls
Victoria Falls, Zimbabwe
Home / Our Lodges / Masuwe Lodge, Victoria Falls
Seolo Africa is proud to partner with Masuwe Lodge, a fan-favourite on Zimbabwe’s Landela Safaris circuit. Masuwe Lodge is the perfect safari holiday destination for those visiting Africa and has the mighty Victoria Falls on their to-see list. With an accumulative safari experience of over 100 years, the Masuwe Lodge staff are more than able to provide an exquisite African safari holiday experience for all. Combining the best of both worlds – the splendour of the Victoria Falls and the mighty Zambezi River surrounded by the Zambezi National Park.
View the website
What activities can you do at Masuwe Lodge
Masuwe Lodge is ideal for those looking to have a place to rest in-between fun-filled activities in the surrounding wilderness. Enjoy a good book by the pool, or take a stroll around the lodge – spotting the countless creatures and critters that call this little piece of heaven home.
Tour of Victoria Falls
Morning and evening safari game drives in the Chamabonda Vlei
Bird watching
Sundowner Cruises
Guided early morning and evening walks on the Masuwe Sanctuary
Whitewater rafting on the Zambezi River
Ziplining
Bungee jump over the Zambezi
Bridge swing over the Zambezi
Helicopter ride over Victoria Falls
Indulge in a massage
What accommodation & amenities are on offer?
Masuwe Lodge features three types of accommodation to suit any visiting party, from wilderness tents for couples through to the private family nest suitable for the whole Brady Bunch!
Wilderness Tents
Masuwe Lodge has nine wilderness tents made of thatch and canvas, featuring an attached stone bathroom that has a shower, a toilet and vanity basin. There’s a viewing deck attached to each wilderness tent, a king-sized or twin single beds, mosquito netting and coffee/tea station. Watch the sunrise from the comfort of your bed as you prepare for an activity-filled day in and around Masuwe Lodge!
The Hide-Away
Honeymooners, this one is for you! Anyone looking for a more private safari getaway can book the hide-away unit. Nestled away in the bush overlooking a small water hole, the Masuwe Hide-Away features a double indoor shower, an outdoor bathtub big enough for two, and a minibar stocked with beverages of your choosing!
The Family Nest
Built from stone and thatch, the Masuwe Family Nest is a two-bedroom private unit spacious enough for larger groups of visitors. Both rooms are en-suite, and the upstairs master bedroom has a private relaxation area should guests wish to escape from the kids for a while. There is a communal living area downstairs, kitchenette with minibar, a shaded deck, plunge pool and a large braai (BBQ) area.
Experience Victoria Falls like few ever do
Only 7 kilometres away from Victoria Falls and a stone’s throw away from the bustling, culturally-vibrant town of Victoria Falls. Make the most of your trip to Zimbabwe with a Masuwe Lodge stay-over! Simply contact Seolo Africa inquire about availability and rates – we look forward to welcoming you to Africa!
Book Now

Practical advice for planning and preparing for your Seolo Africa safari

Travel recommendations
Should I take Malaria tablets when travelling to southern Africa?
The Kruger National Park – Rhino Post Safari Lodge, Plains Camp @ Rhino Walking Safaris and Sleep-Outs – and the Zambezi National Park – Chundu Island – are all situated in malaria areas and we recommend guests err on the side of caution.
One of the best ways to avoid contracting malaria is not to be bitten, so use the insect repellents provided by the lodges, generously and often. Long sleeves and light colours are recommended for evening wear.
Please take the anti-malarial prophylactics recommended by your doctor.
What documents do children need when travelling to or from South Africa?
Before travelling, check the current entry and exit requirements for every child in your party. The documents required may depend on nationality, who the child is travelling with and your travel arrangements.
Consult the official South African Department of Home Affairs guidance and confirm requirements with your airline before departure. If your journey includes Zimbabwe or another country, check that country’s requirements too.
More about travel requirements
National Parks
What is a private concession?
A private concession is an area within a national park which has been put out to tender to be developed and managed by a private enterprise for a specified period.
Rhino Post Safari Lodge and Plains Camp @ Rhino Walking Safaris in the Kruger National Park and Chundu Island in the Zambezi National Park are private concessions that operate within National Parks and pay a concession fee, which provides much-needed income for conservation.
What are conservation fees?
The national parks charge daily conservation fees to all people entering and staying in a national park – whether they are staying in a private concession or the national park’s accommodation. These fees go toward conservation and anti-poaching costs which are not covered by the accommodation rates.
Children and Seolo
Which lodges welcome children?
Children are welcome at several of our lodges, with different age requirements for accommodation and safari activities:
Rhino Post Safari Lodge: Children of all ages are welcome. Children under six require a private vehicle to join game drives. Babysitting is available by prior arrangement.
Chundu Island: Children aged six and older are welcome. Younger children may be accommodated by special arrangement. Guided walks and canoeing are restricted to guests aged 16 and older.
Plains Camp at Rhino Walking Safaris: The standard minimum age for a stay is 12, reflecting the camp’s focus on guided walking safaris.
Please visit each lodge’s FAQs for its full child policy, or contact our reservations team to discuss the best option for your family.
Staying at our lodges
Is the tap water safe to drink?
The tap water is safe to drink at Rhino Post Safari Lodge and Plains Camp @ Rhino Walking Safaris in the Kruger National Park. The tap water at Chundu Island is not potable. Filtered water is freely available at all of our lodges, and while we do not encourage the excessive use of plastic, bottled water is also available.
What is the difference between your Kruger National Park lodges?
Our company name is Rhino Walking Safaris (Pty) Ltd – so named because of our vision of providing specialist walking safaris and authentic wilderness experiences, over and above the traditional game drive safari.
Rhino Post Safari Lodge provides game drive safaris. Plains Camp @ Rhino Walking Safaris and the Sleep-Out decks (branded as Rhino Walking Safaris) focus on walking trails. Many of our guests opt to enjoy all three experiences – game drives, walking safaris and the sleep-outs.
Is tipping expected and how much should I give?
We are frequently asked to recommend a gratuity policy.
While gratuities for exceptional service are very gratefully received by our staff they are at your sole discretion. We do not wish to make a recommendation, because we feel that this places pressure on the guest to pay a specific gratuity; however, if it is of help to you:
At Rhino Walking Safaris and Rhino Post Safari Lodge – the average tips received are between R200 and R350 per room per night for the guides and the same again for the general staff.
At Chundu Island the average tips received are approximately $10 per room per night for the guides, which we allocate according to which activities you have partaken in, with which guide, and the same again for the general staff.
If you do wish to pay a gratuity, you may do so at the reception on checkout. This can be left in cash or credit card. The gratuities for the guides are usually given directly to the guide, and for the general staff to the manager at check out.
General staff gratuities are divided equally amongst all personnel other than the guides.
DO YOUR SAFARI VEHICLES DRIVE OFF-ROAD?
No. Our safari vehicles stay on designated roads to help protect vegetation, minimise disturbance to wildlife and comply with national park requirements. Responsible wildlife viewing is central to our approach. We give animals space and enjoy observing their natural behaviour.
